The Brain is your intelligent memorization assistant. It uses a scientific model (FSRS) to predict how well you remember every page.

● Stability (Colors): Green means the page is solid in your memory. Yellow/Red means it is fading and needs revision soon.

● Symmetry: The app rewards you more if you revise a page right before you forget it. Revising too early provides a smaller boost to long-term memory.

● Forecast Slider: Move the slider at the top to travel through time! See which pages will turn red in 7, 14, or 30 days if you don't revise them.

● Semantic Interference: If you struggle with a verse in the Vault (Mutashabihat), the app automatically lowers the stability of similar verses elsewhere, as they are likely confusion points.

● Revision Debt: The number of pages that have fallen below 50%% stability.

● Recovery Goal: The number of pages you need to revise daily to turn your entire Brain green within a month.

How the app works, and when a page changes level
and when a page moves between weak, fair and strong

It knows what you marked as memorised, the level you gave each juz, and the revisions you log. It never shows one opaque score; it shows what actually happened, and all of it is what you report yourself.

Each page starts at the level you chose for its juz in the memorised screen: weak, fair or strong. With no choice it is fair. That is your estimate, not evidence, so your revision history takes over as it builds up.

• A page becomes weak if you could not complete it last time, or needed help in two of your last three attempts.
• It keeps its starting level while there is little evidence: one successful attempt is not enough to promote it.
• It becomes strong when you recall it yourself (independently or self-corrected) on two different days and your last two attempts were both successful. If those successes span thirty days or more it is “stable over time”.
• Reading or listening only is recorded but never changes the level.

A page you rated fair:
1. Independent recall today → stays fair (still settling).
2. Independent recall three days later → becomes strong.
3. “Could not complete” → back to weak, and revised often.
4. Independent recall on two different days → strong again.
How the plan uses the level

Weak pages come around often and strong ones rarely. In Edit plan you choose how many pages a day each level gets, and the app picks the least recently revised in each. When you log a revision you see its effect on the level before you save.

The memory model (FSRS) estimates how many days your recall holds at 90%. It changes with each revision and colours the memory map, but it does not change a page\'s level in the plan by itself; the level comes from the recall history as described above.
